title: Durable resource and integration recovery inventory providers
description: Objective: supply the missing production recovery-window enumeration sources for scheduler resource effects and integration attempts so the recovery coordinator never infers absence from a generic event scan or a fixture. Deliverable: durable resource and integration attempt inventory records/readers bound to project, effect intent, cursor window and current recovery incarnation, plus immutable RecoveryInventoryRegistration fragments or an equally explicit typed bridge the daemon can compose with @moe/runner registrations. MEASURED GAP at HEAD c0c5929: @moe/scheduler exposes ResourceRow transition functions but no durable inventory enumerator/reader; there is no production integration-attempt record or integration inventory surface in scheduler/store/daemon, and store schema/root probes find no resource/integration inventory rows. The runner collector rejects unknown/extra class evidence. Consumer: task-cf7fb147bd1c47698cbd65c9535370aa. NOT in scope: node-side adapters, adoption/quarantine decisions, project embargo, caller-selected current binding, or recovery.complete. Owned paths: focused scheduler/store contracts and daemon-facing adapters selected after re-measurement; do not grow existing >250-line files. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler test && pnpm --filter @moe/store test && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test && pnpm typecheck.
definitionOfDone: A production durable reader enumerates every project-tagged scheduler resource effect in an exact backup-cursor window, including QUARANTINED/non-fenceable states, and binds each row to its effect intent and source proof digest; empty is COMPLETE only with a verifiable negative proof.

A production durable integration-attempt record and reader enumerate every project-tagged integration target/effect in the same window with exact intent/incarnation binding; unmatched, malformed, duplicate, truncated, or unreadable records stay UNKNOWN with stable code and originating layer.

The daemon-facing bridge exposes immutable registration fragments for the resource and integration populations without mutable global registration, caller-provided item lists, or reimplementation of scheduler/store authority.

Persistence/reopen tests prove resource and integration rows survive process/store reopen and are filtered by exact project/cursor/incarnation; refusal tests assert exact stable code and layer and generated class/case sweeps assert non-zero cardinality.
Focused mutation drills alter each production completeness/fenceability comparison and turn the named resource or integration test red.
Fresh pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler test && pnpm --filter @moe/store test && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test && pnpm typecheck exits 0, with repo-wide foreign red disclosed by owned-path baseline.
taskRails: Do not infer durable inventory from caller-supplied fixtures or by scanning generic events without a typed complete-population contract.
Do not convert restored counters or a caller-selected incarnation into recovery authority; bind to the selected store/anchor current binding.
Missing/unreadable/partial enumeration stays UNKNOWN and preserves the precise upstream code/layer.
If shared schema or wire contracts change, run full regression as required by the global schema rail.
Target <=250 physical lines per production source and split before 400; the cap is per file.

implementationPlan.description: Write the failing acceptance suite first. Using real public scheduler transitions (not hand-built row authority), a file-backed `SqliteEventStore`, the production recovery-incarnation/anchor APIs, and bare workspace imports, cover: all generated resource states including QUARANTINED and `fenceable:false`; multiple integration targets/attempts; exact effect-intent/source-proof binding; seal/reopen equality; exact project/start-excluded/end-included cursor, backup-generation, and current-incarnation filtering; immutable exact two-class fragments; and COMPLETE-empty only with a verified negative proof. Add hostile/missing/unmatched/malformed/duplicate/truncated/unreadable cases asserting the exact existing upstream code and `INVENTORY_ADAPTER` layer, including zero accessor/proxy trap hits. Each class/state/refusal sweep must assert its generated count is nonzero. Name focused tests for the later completeness and fenceability mutation drills, and demonstrate the focused file is red before production implementation.

Implement the exact durable contract and canonical codec. Define the closed `RESOURCE | INTEGRATION_TARGET` vocabulary, caller basis (project tag plus backup cursor/generation only), internal selected scope (store project plus anchored incarnation/key epoch/binding digest), resource and integration observation unions, window seal, immutable class fragment, and typed registration shapes. Caller inputs must have exact own enumerable data keys and cannot contain current refs, counters, item arrays, or authority fields. Canonical bytes use one field order, bounded sizes/counts, deterministic code-point ordering, a body digest, semantic revalidation before digest acceptance, and byte-for-byte re-encode checks. Reuse the daemon's already-admitted stable upstream tuples: invalid input, missing record/seal, unreadable/noncanonical bytes, duplicate/conflict/count mismatch, truncated coverage, and binding mismatch remain UNKNOWN at `INVENTORY_ADAPTER`; add no new authority or disposition. Keep the TS source <=250 lines and add the exact one-line LF runtime bridge.

Implement the durable provider over the public store surface, with no SQLite/schema access. On every append, seal, and read, derive project identity from `getHealth`, read the ACTIVE recovery binding, read the matching daemon anchor, and require exact incarnation/key epoch/binding/generation agreement; never accept those refs from the caller. Persist one canonical observation per call through deterministic `commitExpectedVersionDecision` identities into a dedicated aggregate addressed by project, backup cursor/generation, and current incarnation. Snapshot `ResourceRow` exhaustively (including state, capacity, epoch, external, and a closed FENCEABLE/NON_FENCEABLE projection) without reimplementing scheduler transitions; bind resource identity as `(resourceId,effectIntentRef)`. Bind integration identity as `(attemptRef,targetRef,effectIntentRef)` plus intent digest and source proof. Replay identical writes, refuse divergent duplicates, and serialize append versus seal by expected aggregate version so no post-seal row can succeed.

Complete the same provider with the sealed reader and daemon composition seam. Seal only after reading and validating all typed aggregate rows; require exactly one source coverage proof for each of the two classes, compute per-class nonzero cardinality/ordered row-digest commitments, require a bound negative proof for a zero-row class, and commit one terminal seal whose stored global position is the inclusive window end. Read only the dedicated aggregate with bounded pagination, require exact sequence/decision trace/event types, canonical bytes, unique identities, one final seal, exact counts/digests, and positions `(backupCursor,endInclusive]`; missing/partial/unreadable evidence returns the precise UNKNOWN tuple and never a partial list. Export a frozen literal two-registration tuple/factory whose enumerators accept only basis/window, recheck the selected binding, return frozen raw observations plus proof fragments, and never decide adoption, quarantine, signing authority, or `recovery.complete`; no mutable global registry or caller item list. Keep the production source <=250 lines and the `.js` bridge exactly one LF-terminated export line.

Run the single concentrated verification gate. First run the focused daemon test, then perform two reversible mutation drills against the production surface: weaken the seal completeness/count comparison and alter the ResourceRow fenceability projection; in each case assert the specifically named focused test exits nonzero, count both drills (nonzero), reverse only that owned patch without `git restore/reset`, and confirm the original bytes return. Check no probe/debug/generated evidence remains. Then run exactly `pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler test && pnpm --filter @moe/store test && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test && pnpm typecheck` fresh in the foreground and record exit status/output. Compare failures with the pre-diff baseline and disclose foreign red verbatim; completion requires no new failing path intersecting these five owned paths.

Load `adversarial-self-review` and inspect the complete owned-path diff as an attacker: concurrent/replayed append versus seal, empty/huge/duplicate arrays, wrong cursor/project/generation, stale or absent ACTIVE binding/anchor, hostile descriptors/proxies, digest/order ambiguity, partial pagination, post-seal writes, non-fenceable and QUARANTINED omission, integration identity collisions, accidental mutable/global state, and any path that could emit authority from UNKNOWN. Verify Windows handles close before cleanup and both production files remain <=250 lines (split before 400 only via replan). If review changes bytes, rerun the exact gate above. Finally run `git status --porcelain`, unstage any foreign staged path, commit only with the explicit five-path pathspec, verify `git show --stat` contains only owned paths, record downstream consumer `task-cf7fb147bd1c47698cbd65c9535370aa`, and call `moe.complete_task`; if QA rejects, address only the pinned rejection and rerun the same gate.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Use the task's explicit 'equally explicit typed bridge' option, implemented inside the daemon over the existing public SqliteEventStore decision/event API. Rejected widening @moe/runner: its RecoveryInventoryRegistration class union is intentionally frozen to four node-side classes and cannot represent RESOURCE or INTEGRATION_TARGET. Rejected dedicated SQLite tables/schema v5: it would add migration/schema ownership without improving the required post-restore inventory proof and would exceed this task's focused file budget. The selected design uses one dedicated, incarnation-addressed aggregate with typed row events and a terminal two-class seal; reads use readAggregateEvents for that aggregate only. Rejected adding scheduler persistence: ResourceRow already is the scheduler authority, so the daemon snapshots that public type without duplicating its transitions.

planningNotes.risks: The seal must prove exact cardinality/order for both classes; `every()` without a two-class count is vacuous. A seal digest by itself is not completeness unless it binds the typed source proofs, row identities/digests, project, backup cursor/generation, selected anchor/incarnation/key epoch, and exact end cursor. Concurrent append/seal must use expected-version serialization so a row cannot appear after a successful seal. Duplicate identity is (resourceId,effectIntentRef) for resources and (attemptRef,targetRef,effectIntentRef) for integrations, preserving distinct attempts while refusing conflicting repeats. No bridge result may decide ADOPTED/QUARANTINED or grant recovery.complete. Keep both new production TS files <=250 physical lines; exact one-line LF .js bridges are required. File-backed reopen tests must close every SQLite handle before Windows temp-directory cleanup. Consumer composition remains task-cf7fb147bd1c47698cbd65c9535370aa; do not treat that downstream blocked task as a prerequisite.
